title: SKY WHALE
note: All times in seconds from film start. Frame n covers t = n/48. Shots are [start,end) in frames. Cues are visual events the sound must sync to; both the renderer and the audio pipeline read this file.

shots.desc: Dawn crane: cloud sea at first light, swell, breakout, breach, pull back to full scale against sunrise
shots.whaleDistance: 350 m under cloud (muffled) -> 180 m open air

shots.desc: High wide over patchwork valley 1 km below; whale small
Close on the great pectoral fin stroking through the air
Whale swims into a towering cream cloud bank and is swallowed
Into the storm: light dies to slate, rain begins
Inside the storm cloud, labouring; lightning lights the whale
Bursts out of the top of the storm into sunlight under a rainbow
shots.whaleDistance: 100 m, inside cloud -> open air at 53.2

shots.desc: Calm dusk sea, whale low over the water: breath, blow, call, held stillness (ma)
HARD CUT on the silence: extreme lonely wide, tiny whale swims across the sun road. No answer.
Locked-off moonlit wide; the Old Whale crosses alone
Close: the Old Whale sings under the moon
Distant eyes appear; the pod rises one by one; Old Whale joins; slow pull back; together toward the moon; hold

cues.desc: cloud sea starts to bulge (whale rising beneath)
first waking song, from inside the cloud: muffled, distant
snout tears through the cloud surface (far cloud-break accent)
brow emerges
brass eye clears the cloud and catches the sun
garden, pine and mast emerge; pennants unfurl
fins open like breath (timber creak of spars)
blowhole exhale: warm vapour plume
breach into golden sky; musical bloom peaks here
waking song in open air, clear
contented hum, far above the valley
fin downstroke (subtle air accent)
spars creak at bottom of stroke
second downstroke
spars creak
short breath before entering cloud
snout enters the cloud bank; sound muffles progressively until 38.2
rain streaks begin (visual only, no rain bed)
effort groan
lightning strike 1 (lights the whale)
effort groan, labouring
lightning strike 2 (double flicker)
effort groan, rising
lightning strike 3, biggest
whale bursts out of the storm top (storm-burst air accent)
lifts clear into sunlight under a rainbow: relief
relieved exhale
draws a breath (intake)
blows: soft translucent vapour plume
THE CALL: head lifts, eye brightens; lasts to ~66.6
held stillness; call tail decays; true digital silence from 67.9
HARD CUT on the silence to extreme lonely wide; silence continues
moonlit cloud sea, Old Whale crosses alone
the Old Whale sings under the moon (lasts to ~86.0)
warm points of light (eyes) appear along the distant cloud band
Drover rises (far cloud-break, deep voice)
Pip rises (small, young voice)

together they swim toward the moon; music resolves
